medicare_estimate_how.text: Medicom’s Medicare estimates follow CMS’s 2026 physician fee schedule formula: each service’s relative value units, adjusted for New Jersey costs, times the conversion factor. CMS set the 2026 conversion factor at $33.40 for most clinicians.

sources.title: Medicare Physician Fee Schedule relative value files, RVU26D
Calendar Year (CY) 2026 Medicare Physician Fee Schedule Final Rule (CMS-1832-F)

medicare_facility_rate.text: CMS uses a separate facility rate for services in hospitals, emergency rooms, skilled nursing facilities and surgery centers, and a non-facility rate everywhere else, such as a doctor’s office.

sources.title: Medicare Physician Fee Schedule relative value files, RVU26D

price_transparency_list.text: Federal rules require hospitals to publish online a list of their standard charges for all items and services.

sources.title: Hospital price transparency
sources.authority: U.S. Department of Health and Human Services

price_transparency_shoppable.text: Hospitals must also show prices for at least 300 shoppable services in a consumer-friendly way, or offer an online price estimator.

sources.title: Hospital price transparency
sources.authority: U.S. Department of Health and Human Services

price_terms.text: In those lists, the gross charge is the hospital’s chargemaster price before any discounts, and the discounted cash price is what applies to someone paying cash.

disclaimer: Medicare amounts are a reference point, not what you owe. Your coverage, the hospital’s contracts and its financial assistance rules decide what you pay. A difference from the Medicare amount is context for a question, not evidence that a charge is wrong.
